newsitem.title: UK: Stg firm, sticks to narrow ranges ahead of BOE.
newsitem.headline: Stg firm, sticks to narrow ranges ahead of BOE.

text.p: Sterling hovered around the 2.97 mark level in European morning trading, slightly up from Wednesday's close, as dealers awaited an announcement on interest rates by the Bank of England.

The pound came under profit-taking pressure overnight, touching a low at 2.9635 marks but recovered as the market did not have the stomach to take it lower ahead of the rate announcement at 1100 GMT, traders said.
A rate rise looked like a foregone conclusion as the BOE was expected to tighten credit further in a bid to quench robust consumer spending.
"A quarter point interest rate rise is firmly factored into the pound, and only a 50 basis points might spur the pound into action to extend its rally," said a trader at a UK bank.

At 0900 GMT the pound was at 2.9703/13 marks and $1.6858 compared with 2.9671/81 and $1.6844/49 in late European trading on Wednesday. Some analysts argued though that the committee does not need to take stringent action and that the market is overestimating inflationary pressures. "We expect a 25 basis points tightening, but we see the risks of no tightening being much greater than the risks of a 50 basis points move," economists at Chase said in a note to clients. Some dealers see an increasing risk of a sterling correction even if the central bank opts for a 50 basis points rise.

"The problem for the pound is that it has been rising relentlessly without a proper correction," said Mark Ostwald, technical analyst at Monument Derivatives. "There is a risk of a move down all the way to 2.85 marks," he added.

Such a large drop would not rule out an eventual stab at the 3.00 mark level though. Dealers said the pound's trend would remain up, and any correction would be a welcome opportunity to pick it up at lower levels.
